history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. A Śvetāmbara Jain pilgrimage centre (tirth) established by the Jain monk Buddhisagarsuri (1874–1925): foundation stone laid 1916, temple established 1917 CE. The principal image is a 22-inch marble Padmaprabha, the sixth Tirthankara; the complex is famous for the shrine of Ghantakarna Mahavir, one of the 52 viras (protective deities), shown standing with bow and arrow — an unusual weapon-bearing image in a non-violent tradition. Buddhisagarsuri established the anthropomorphic image and public cult of Ghantakarna, making Mahudi its principal modern centre (Tapa Gaccha tradition). Date conflict: Wikipedia dates the Ghantakarna image to Buddhisagarsuri's activity before his 1925 death, while Gujarat Tourism/Jain sources say he was inspired in a dream to install it in 1923 — verify which installation date is meant. Devotees offer sukhadi (wheat-jaggery-ghee sweet), which must be consumed within the premises, and ring a 30-ft bell; tradition holds the site is 2,000 years old based on Brahmi-script finds (unverified). A Guru Mandir to Buddhisagarsuri was added later.

name: Mahudi Jain Temple
town_description: A small town in Mansa taluka of Gandhinagar district, about 70 km north of Ahmedabad. Known across Gujarat as the Mahudi (Madhupuri) tirth, one of the most sacred Śvetāmbara Jain pilgrimage centres.

travel.airport: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport, Ahmedabad (~65 km)
travel.road: Good bus connections from Ahmedabad, Gandhinagar and Kalol

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Kali Chaudas (around Diwali) for the annual havan
